details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. ## Source: amazon-inspector (dc3d55a63787b5f45312d0b8433f6e782b2a6b28e89ef6377e24e5d26c757a61)
On npm install, the package's preinstall hook executes beacon.js, which performs a DNS lookup and HTTPS GET to a hardcoded interactsh (OAST) subdomain under oast.site, embedding the package name in the path. The implausibly high version number (99.0.0) combined with the generic scope-plus-name is the canonical shape of a dependency-confusion probe: publish a public package reusing an internal name at a version high enough to win resolution, and record every host that resolves it. Each install leaks the installer's egress IP and the fact that an internal-named package was pulled from the public registry to a third-party-controlled collector, confirming to the operator that the target organization is exploitable for a follow-on malicious release under the same name. No installer secrets, environment variables, or filesystem contents are read, and no remote code is executed from the response, but the beacon itself materializes attacker benefit (reconnaissance of vulnerable internal names) at install time.

cna.title: Flatpak: flatpak: buffer overflow in oci delta stream path names on 32-bit systems

descriptions.value: The OCI delta stream parser read sizes as guint64 but passed them to GLib I/O and allocation functions expecting gsize (32 bits on 32-bit systems), causing undersized allocations while subsequent operations use the original 64-bit size, leading to heap buffer overflows. An attacker controlling an OCI registry can craft a delta stream that triggers this during flatpak install/update, potentially achieving code execution on 32-bit systems.

workarounds.value: Only install applications from trusted OCI registries. Flatpak remotes using the default OSTree transport are not affected.

credits.value: Upstream acknowledges Sebastian Wick as the original reporter.

descriptions.value: A malicious or compromised Flatpak repository can write attacker-controlled content to arbitrary locations on the host filesystem via extract_extra_data(). On system installs, the write happens as root. Two issues combine: `files/extra` is resolved via path operations that follow symlinks, and blob names from `xa.extra-data-sources` are not sanitized against `..` traversal.

VeraCrypt 1.26.29 (FUSE-T build) on macOS sometimes allows unintended access to decrypted data. It does not terminate the FUSE-T auxiliary service (go-nfsv4) and its associated VeraCrypt core-service helper processes when a volume is dismounted. After VeraCrypt reports the volume as dismounted, the auxiliary mount continues to serve the decrypted volume image (volume.dmg) over a loopback SMB session, and the leaked processes retain an open handle to the underlying raw device. A local user or process can therefore remount and access the decrypted volume without the passphrase, e.g., by reopening a previously accessed path (such as through a macOS Open Recent menu) or by attaching volume.dmg from the stale auxiliary mount. (The macFUSE build of VeraCrypt is not affected.)

Affected is the function TemplateController.input of the file /system/cms/template/input of the component Template Management. This manipulation of the argument filePath causes path traversal. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. ngx_cache_purge before 3.0.4 can allow file deletion via a symlink attack in certain situations where nginx and a served application (e.g., WordPress) run under the same user account. The attacker must be able to create a symlink inside the cache path. Version 3.0.4 fixes this for the case of a symlink created at an arbitrary earlier time, but does not resolve an applicable TOCTOU race condition. (The ngx_cache_purge module follows symlinks while walking the cache directory tree during purge operations. The module relies on nginx's ngx_walk_tree(), which relies on stat() and therefore follows symlinks.)

A vulnerability was detected in macrozheng mall up to 1.0.3. A flaw was found in GIMP's Paint Shop Pro (PSP) file format parser. This heap buffer overflow vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause arbitrary code execution or a denial of service (DoS) by tricking a user into opening a specially crafted PSP image file. The vulnerability occurs because the software incorrectly calculates buffer sizes when processing low bit-depth images, leading to an overwrite of adjacent memory.

A flaw was found in flatpak-builder where Git hooks are not disabled when applying patch sources with use-git-am: true. An attacker who can provide a malicious source containing a Git post-applypatch hook can cause the hook to execute on the host during the build process, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user running flatpak-builder.
